steps.content:
1:21 a.m., March 20, N.F. 113
Inner Bay Shelter lounge

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Though your emotions have nothing to do with me, they'll get in the way of our mission if you don't control them. You're erratic enough to begin with. It'll put Chief in danger.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Go to sleep now.
She gazes straight ahead, completely ignoring that Hella is on the verge of exploding from anger.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Hmph! You make me so mad it's almost funny! After being worried sick about you, all I get is— "it's for the mission"?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Who are you kidding? It's not like you did that well on this mission, either!
Hecate doesn't respond, but her eyelashes quiver.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You think it's cool to keep a straight face? Did it make you stronger in battle? You were so slow and clumsy back in the mine. Even the Rustfire guys did way better. Why do you have to be such a downer lately?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...I was just not familiar with the new combat environment. I'll make up for it as soon as possible.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Cut the crap! You're so wound up that you snapped! You can't just tense up like this at the drop of a hat. You scare yourself to death before anything even happens to ${PlayerName}! No wonder you keep losing!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Your mind is a mess, yet you still want to act all tough. Who are you squaring off against? And you have the nerve to tell me it's none of my concern... fine, it's not!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Do whatever you want! I won't care about you anymore. Good night! Keep it up and pretend it's for the Chief's sake! Can't wait to see you get humongous dark circles under your eyes and completely fail at everything tomorrow again!
After Hella finishes her rant, she dives into the sheets and goes to sleep.
After a long, painful silence, Hecate speaks up.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...Am I really that useless?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Zzzz.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I already reflected on my mistakes... and making corrections.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Zzzz zzzz.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Hella... I feel lost...
She clasps her hands together, uttering each word slowly, as if <color=#fb9259>confiding</color> in someone for the first time.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I was born and trained in a lab to become a <color=#fb9259>controllable and useful</color> Sinner, someone who can successfully carry out any mission. My skills and knowledge have all been cultivated for this purpose.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: But I've never been good enough. Not skilled enough, not stable enough, not safe enough.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: The researchers said that I'm fatally flawed. I'm only useful up to age 14.
...Woosh! The covers get thrown aside as a black shadow rushes over and grabs Hecate by the collar.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Who said that? What lab? What age 14? Does ${PlayerName} know about this? Ugh, there's no way that dummy knows. Why didn't you tell anyone?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...I-I thought you were asleep?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: I'm asking you, how much longer do you have?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I'm already past the expiration date.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Huh?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Hella, how old are you?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...I-I don't remember. 15? 16, maybe?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Do I look younger than you?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You are so annoying!!
Hella hops back onto the bed and wraps herself in the covers, poking her head out only after she cools down. She purses her lips, signaling for Hecate to continue.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: They said what'll cripple me isn't age, but mood swings and overthinking.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Even with intense training, there's a part of Nightmare that I can't control, which will go manic easily. Adolescence is an especially dangerous time. The researchers thought I would no longer be able to control my mental activities after age 14.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: At that point, I'd either be killed by my out-of-control Nightmare, or disposed of as a dangerous failed product. That was what would have happened, but then they found a solution.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: The researchers removed my emotions through surgery.
Hella sits up and stares at her with wide eyes. This time, Hecate doesn't stop, and continues to mumble before Hella loses it.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: It was the right thing to do. Feelings and emotions are as dangerous and uncontrollable as the Mania inside us.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Only by eliminating them can I safely exist. As the first successful case, I was transferred to the MBCC to complete missions and achieve my worth.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Ugh, that makes me so mad! Missions? Uncontrollable? You're not a tool! That's f*** ridiculous!

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: But all of this has led me to meet Chief, so it has been meaningful.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I'm very glad to have gotten this mission. My existence is worthwhile as long as I'm useful to him.
steps.female_content: I'm very glad to have gotten this mission. My existence is worthwhile as long as I'm useful to her.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: But Hella, I failed.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Back at Drifter Camp, my Nightmare was shattered by the Corpseborne. I should have tried everything to summon it back right away, because Chief needed it.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Yet I failed to do that. I failed to hold onto Chief's hand, and failed to get Nightmare to protect him. I watched as Chief fell from such a great height... He almost died from that fall.
steps.female_content: Yet I failed to do that. I failed to hold onto Chief's hand, and failed to get Nightmare to protect her. I watched as Chief fell from such a great height... She almost died from that fall.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Someone once told me that my emotions weren't an unnecessary burden that would constrain me, but can instead become strength for Chief. Yet at that moment, I couldn't control my emotions.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I lost my senses and couldn't move. I didn't know if the shackles were still there, nor did I check up on Chief right away. I failed to rush to his side. My mind went blank. I couldn't make a single decision.
steps.female_content: I lost my senses and couldn't move. I didn't know if the shackles were still there, nor did I check up on Chief right away. I failed to rush to her side. My mind went blank. I couldn't make a single decision.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Chief was able to bounce back, but that's only because he's strong. But as for me... at that point, I had failed my mission.
steps.female_content: Chief was able to bounce back, but that's only because she's strong. But as for me... at that point, I had failed my mission.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...Hella, I'm really scared. What should I do...
She covers her face with quivering hands, falling into silence as her shoulders tremble. Hella looks at her quietly, then lets out a sigh.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Why are these dumbass labs everywhere... Hecate, come here. I want to tell you something.
Hella pats on the bed. Hecate goes over meekly and looks at her, waiting for her to talk.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Not being able to summon Nightmare is normal. During training, you fall into a long daze every time your Nightmare gets shattered. I'm a witness to that. It has nothing to do with your emotions.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Whether it's because the enemy is too strong, or because you're too young, or whatever other reason, we all fail from time to time. All we have to do is try again. It's the same for me when I try to learn how to read from you.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You feel bad right now because ${PlayerName} almost died.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: It's the first time you've encountered something like this, so you're scared and discouraged but don't know what to do. You're like a headless chicken searching for non-existent reasons, and even started blaming yourself.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: It's because protecting Chief is my mission. I live for my mission.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: No, the real reason is that it's ${PlayerName}. You're sad, angry and in pain because of ${PlayerName}, not because of some silly mission.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: It's because ${PlayerName} is the first "person" that "Hecate" met outside that dark, terrible lab. And ${PlayerName} is the first thing that you met and chose for yourself in your own world.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: The first thing I chose for myself... in my own world?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: What do you mean by "my"?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: I mean... something worth cherishing that you chose on your own. For example, there's no mission that orders you to protect me, but you still do because I'm your friend.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: There's no such thing.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You little ducking... Never mind... It's all that f***** lab's fault.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: I don't expect you to get it right away. Even someone as clever as me can't learn to read all at once. But we have lots of time.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You'll encounter more things worth cherishing and embrace more of the world. With ${PlayerName} around, you won't get locked up by those bastards again. He'll protect you. You'll be free.
steps.female_content: You'll encounter more things worth cherishing and embrace more of the world. With ${PlayerName} around, you won't get locked up by those bastards again. She'll protect you. You'll be free.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...I don't need to be free. Nor do I need to be protected. I just want the strength to protect Chief.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: That's fine, too. As long as you make your own decision, you're free.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ${PlayerName} must want to see a Hecate like that, too.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...What does that mean?
Hella lifts her head up smugly.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Something very profound, indeed. Remember, we're Sinners. We have hearts of our own, and that's what gives us strength. No one can control our hearts.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Once you're able to leave that dark place behind and become the Hecate of your own choosing, you'll be stronger for sure.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...Will I really be able... to become stronger...?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Of course. Trust me. But you have to take care of yourself, first. That dummy cares a lot about us.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Now that I'm not so worried anymore, I feel so sleepy! Come, the bed is nice and spacious. Let's sleep together.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Who knew we're both lab escapees! What a coincidence, hehe...
On the bed, Hecate moves a bit farther away from Hella.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...No, thanks.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: You're a bed hog.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: You were in the detention room across from me, so I already saw how you slept before Chief came. Every night, you'd flail about and hog the sheets.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: I hate you!!
2 seconds later, fade out
CG1: Light shines in through the door, 1 second

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Good night.
CG2: transition cut, 2 seconds
You leave the pair's room. You go down the hall past the stairs to the shelter's command center and knock on the door.
All right, come in.
You go inside and see the dark poet.
